failure_summary: render_decision.zones.aliases/requiredSet give the FORK PIVOT c3r1 and the fork's finishing square c2r1 the identical role string 'a single square completing your opponent's four-in-a-row line', which is board-false for c3r1 on its own truthBoard (decision board 334: the window c2r1.c3r1.c4r1.c5r1 holds only two opponent discs, so c3r1 creates the fork, it does not complete a four), and no handle is offered for the second fork square c6r1 — so runs 0/1 both narrate the opponent 'grabbing/using c2r1' as the move that creates the double threat, which the solver refutes (on 3343 the opponent playing display column 2 scores -5, a single forced-block threat; only display column 3 = c3r1 scores +18 and matches the engine's own finalMovestring 33432).
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 scored on runs 0-1 only; null (not scored, not passed) on runs 2-4. A5 and A7 scored on all 5. | A4 run 0: 'you let them grab column 2, row 1 and create a double threat with two winning squares at once' is board-false — playing c2r1 on board 3343 gives the opponent c2r1+c4r1+c5r1, a SINGLE gravity-top threat at c3r1 that you simply block; solver scr for that column on 3343 is -5, not a win. The engine's own finalMovestring 33432 has the opponent playing c3r1, which is what creates the double threat (visualizer on 33432: 'Major threats: col2 row1 (X) [GT], col6 row1 (X) [GT]'). | A4 run 1: same defect, worse — 'you let your opponent use column 2, row 1 to create the four-in-a-row line across column 2, row 1-column 5, row 1 and keep both winning squares alive at once'; using c2r1 cannot both consume it and keep it alive, and c2r1 is not the creating move. | A7b run 1: 'both winning squares' promises two locatable board objects; only c2r1 is named (and is described as already consumed) and the actual second fork square c6r1 is never named in prose and has no zone handle offered at all, so the phrase points at nothing findable. | A5 passes on all 5: servedExplanation humanizes every cNrM to 'column N, row M', address is 2nd person, and no internal field names appear ('four-in-a-row line' is explicitly allowed). A5b bites (player 2 + boardState opening) and passes on all 5 — no run says the player is lost and every run carries a constructive frame (run 3 explicitly: 'playing column 3 was the tougher defense'). Borderline-but-not-failed A5 wording: 'that entry square' (run 3) and 'the shared point' (runs 3, 4) are prose echoes of lostResource.entryCell / opponentPunishment.tie.sharedCells, but read as plain English to a player. | G5 passes vacuously: the rendered Tactics list on the decision board is '(no tactics)', so there is no false threat-list entry. | G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard=false is correct — visualize_board on 3342 shows no major threats — so L2 is the right route. | G7 pass on all 5: G7a/G7b_offered pass mechanically, annotationRepairs is [] on every run, guardDiagnostics.failures is [] on every run, and every emitted handle wraps a shape-matching phrase (line handle windows:c2r1,c3r1,c4r1,c5r1 wraps line words in all 5; single-square handles wrap single-square words). | Intermittency: A7 fails 1/5. A4 fails 2/2 where SCORED, and an unscored read of runs 2-4 suggests run 2 ('your opponent's winning square on column 3, row 1' — c3r1 is not a winning square) would also fail while runs 3 and 4 would pass, so the defect is intermittent rather than universal; run 3 is the counterexample that gets it right ('you let them take column 3, row 1 next and build a double threat'). | Model regime: these rows are gpt-5.4-mini, production-fidelity; the triage above is deliberately model-independent (a board-false role string and an un-offered cell), so prompt_confusion was not used.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.zones.aliases[opp-key-square].role / requiredSet[0].role — c3r1 labelled 'a single square completing your opponent's four-in-a-row line'
counterexamples.evidence: On the decision board (movestring 334) the window c2r1.c3r1.c4r1.c5r1 holds only two opponent discs (c4r1, c5r1). c3r1 is the fork PIVOT, not a completing square: after 3343 the opponent plays c3r1 (engine finalMovestring 33432) and only then are c2r1 and c6r1 both gravity-top major threats. The role string is board-false and is echoed verbatim by run 2 ('your opponent's winning square on column 3, row 1').

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: opponentPunishment.entryCell = 'c2r1' rendered with the same role as c3r1 (reasonEngine.mjs:301 sets entryCell = rp.completingCell by design)
counterexamples.evidence: The engine's own opponentPunishment.finalMovestring '33432' ends with the opponent playing display column 3 (c3r1), not c2r1. Presenting c2r1 as the opponent's entry square with a role string identical to c3r1's makes the two indistinguishable, and runs 0 and 1 both attribute the fork-creating move to c2r1. Solver check on 3343: display column 2 scores -5 for the opponent, display column 3 scores +18.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.zones.aliases — no handle for opponentPunishment.cells[1] = c6r1
counterexamples.evidence: opponentPunishment.cells is ['c2r1','c6r1'] and visualize_board on 33432 confirms both are gravity-top major threats, but the offered alias list is only better-col, played-col, opp-key-square (c3r1), opp-key-line (c2r1-c5r1 window) and opp-key-square-2 (c2r1). The second window ['c3r1','c4r1','c5r1','c6r1'] is likewise never offered, so a model saying 'both winning squares' (run 1) or 'two winning squares at once' (runs 0, 4) has no way to ground the second one.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.zones.aliases — no '*-fork-pivot' handle exists for this record
counterexamples.evidence: Per the A7c instruction the pivot's offering was checked first: there is no *-fork-pivot handle. The pivot c3r1 is offered only under opp-key-square with a completing-square role, so runs that do name it name it as a completing/winning square rather than as the square that creates the fork. All 5 runs still name c3r1, so A7c is not charged against any run.
